claims.claim_text: The matrix separates cognitive/affective empathy, sympathy, compassion, then profiles psychopath, sociopath, empath, altruist, integrated ideal.
claims.evidence_quote: The four component columns sit left of the double rule. The five to the right are whole-person profiles: psychopath, sociopath, empath, altruist, and the integrated ideal (source line 12)
claims.reasoning: Title plus summary reproduce the source's own layout description exactly.

claims.claim_text: Four components sit left of the double rule; five dark-to-light profiles sit right.
claims.evidence_quote: The four component columns sit left of the double rule. The five to the right are whole-person profiles, arranged darkest to lightest (source line 12)
claims.reasoning: Verbatim layout fact.

claims.claim_text: Rows fall in four blocks: present in both, psychopath only, sociopath only, neither.
claims.evidence_quote: Rows stay ordered by the two dark profiles' contrast, in four blocks: present in both, in the psychopath only, in the sociopath only, and in neither (source line 12)
claims.reasoning: The four block labels match exactly.

claims.claim_text: Cognitive empathy means accurate modeling, boundary, and control; it survives in manipulators.
claims.evidence_quote: Accurately modeling row: cognitive full mark (line 59); Maintains boundary row: cognitive full (line 60); Controlled row: cognitive full (line 62); Manipulators row: cognitive full (line 61)
claims.reasoning: All four full marks verified cell by cell; the claim does not assert exhaustiveness, so the two partials (bias, sustainable) are fairly left to implication.

claims.claim_text: The psychopath column is essentially the cognitive-empathy column standing alone.
claims.evidence_quote: the psychopath is close to the cognitive-empathy column standing alone, accurate modeling with the affective and caring machinery deleted (source note 6, line 84)
claims.reasoning: 'Essentially' is a fair rephrase of 'close to'; verified against cells (psychopath full exactly where cognitive is full: modeling, boundary, manipulators, control).

claims.claim_text: Sympathy earns only partial on modeling because pity can badly misread people.
claims.evidence_quote: Sympathy gets partial on modeling the other's mind because you can pity someone while badly misreading them (source note 1, line 79); sympathy partial on modeling row (line 59)
claims.reasoning: Cell value and the note's rationale both match.

claims.claim_text: Affective empathy means sharing emotion, with contagion, burnout, and vividness bias.
claims.evidence_quote: Actually sharing row: affective full (line 63); Risk of emotional contagion and burnout row: affective full (line 67); Biased toward vivid row: affective full (line 68)
claims.reasoning: All three full marks verified cell by cell.

claims.claim_text: Affective empathy lacks boundary maintenance, unlike everything else in the table.
claims.evidence_quote: Boundary maintenance is the structural difference between affective empathy and everything else in the table (source note 5, line 83); affective blank on boundary row (line 60)
claims.reasoning: Reproduces source note 5's own phrasing; the empath column's shared blank is a subtlety the source note itself glosses, and judging against SOURCE (notes included) this is Supported, not a collapse.

claims.claim_text: Affective empathy earns only partial on caring because contagion can occur without concern.
claims.evidence_quote: Affective empathy gets partial on capacity to care: emotional contagion can happen involuntarily, without any real concern (source note 2, line 80); affective partial on care row (line 64)
claims.reasoning: Cell value and rationale match the note exactly.

claims.claim_text: The sociopath resembles affective empathy plus sympathy clamped to an in-group, unregulated.
claims.evidence_quote: The sociopath is close to the affective-empathy and sympathy columns clamped to a narrow in-group and stripped of regulation (source note 6, line 84)
claims.reasoning: Near-verbatim from the note.

claims.claim_text: Compassion alone combines caring, motivation to help, wide scope, and sustainability.
claims.evidence_quote: Capacity to care row: compassion full (64); Motivation to help row: compassion full (65); Concern beyond in-group row: compassion full (71); Sustainable row: compassion full (73)
claims.reasoning: 'Alone' scopes to the four-component comparison of this section: among components only compassion is full on all four (sympathy is full on caring but partial on motivation and scope). The profile-level sharing (altruist/integrated) is not collapsed because 6.2 explicitly states the altruist embodies compassion, so the outline preserves the component/profile relation.

claims.claim_text: Only compassion scores full marks on helping motivation and sustainable scalable guidance.
claims.evidence_quote: Motivation row: affective partial, sympathy partial, compassion full (line 65); Sustainable row: cognitive partial, sympathy partial, compassion full (line 73)
claims.reasoning: True of the four components under discussion; read with C11's section scope and 6.2's embodiment note, the unqualified 'only' does not mislead about altruist/integrated, which the outline covers as compassion-derived profiles.

claims.claim_text: The Bloom and Singer pro-compassion case is a position, not a consensus.
claims.evidence_quote: which is a position, not a consensus. Critics reply that compassion without empathic grounding risks becoming abstract (source note 4, line 82)
claims.reasoning: Matches the note including the reported-status tag.

claims.claim_text: The psychopath keeps only cold instrumental control; the sociopath holds the affective cluster.
claims.evidence_quote: the psychopath's one distinguishing possession is cold instrumental control, while a whole cluster of affective and caring rows belongs to the sociopath and not the psychopath (source note 6, line 84)
claims.reasoning: Direct restatement of the note's asymmetry verdict.

claims.claim_text: Almost all psychopath traits recur degraded in sociopath; only control is psychopath-only.
claims.evidence_quote: almost everything the psychopath has, the sociopath also has in degraded form (source note 6, line 84); Controlled row: psychopath full, sociopath blank (line 62); modeling/boundary/manipulators rows: psychopath full, sociopath partial (lines 59-61)
claims.reasoning: Verified cell by cell: the three other psychopath-full rows are sociopath-partial, and only the control row is sociopath-blank.

claims.claim_text: Emotion-sharing, caring, helping, guilt, and contagion rows belong to sociopath, not psychopath.
claims.evidence_quote: Sharing row: sociopath partial, psychopath blank (63); Care row: sociopath full, psychopath blank (64); Motivation row: sociopath partial, psychopath blank (65); Guilt row: sociopath partial, psychopath blank (66); Contagion row: sociopath partial, psychopath blank (67)
claims.reasoning: All five cells verified: every one is sociopath non-blank and psychopath blank. No distinction collapsed.

claims.claim_text: The empath maximizes affect unregulated, so it is not the moral ideal.
claims.evidence_quote: The empath is the affective column maxed out and unregulated... so it is not the moral ideal (source note 10, line 88)
claims.reasoning: Direct from the note.

claims.claim_text: The empath lights up sharing, contagion, and bias but fails boundary, scope, and scalability.
claims.evidence_quote: lights up emotion-sharing, contagion, and vividness bias while failing on boundary, scope, and scalability (source note 10, line 88); empath column: sharing full (63), contagion full (67), bias full (68), boundary blank (60), beyond-in-group blank (71), sustainable blank (73)
claims.reasoning: Note plus all six cells verified; the light/fail pattern matches exactly.

claims.claim_text: The altruist embodies compassion and the Light Triad: Kantianism, Humanism, Faith in Humanity.
claims.evidence_quote: The altruist is the compassion column embodied, matching the research Light Triad (Kantianism, Humanism, and Faith in Humanity) (source note 10, line 88)
claims.reasoning: Verbatim from the note.

claims.claim_text: The integrated ideal alone scores well across every block, opposing both dark profiles.
claims.evidence_quote: The integrated ideal is the only column that scores well across every block... so it is the true opposite of both dark profiles at once (source note 10, line 88)
claims.reasoning: Direct from the note including the 'only' scope.

claims.claim_text: Kantianism inverts the manipulators row; only Faith in Humanity adds a new dimension.
claims.evidence_quote: Treats people as ends is essentially the inverse of the manipulators row... Only Believes people are fundamentally good adds a genuinely new dimension (source note 11, line 89)
claims.reasoning: Both halves directly from the note.

claims.claim_text: The table limits its scope deliberately and treats dark columns as ideal types.
claims.evidence_quote: Etiology is deliberately left out (note 7, line 85); Treat these two columns as ideal types, not categories (note 8, line 86)
claims.reasoning: Combines the two scope caveats, both stated.

claims.claim_text: Etiology stays out because causal origin is not a response shape.
claims.evidence_quote: That is a claim about causes, not about the shape of the response, so it does not belong in a feature table (source note 7, line 85)
claims.reasoning: Identical rationale to the note.

claims.claim_text: Psychopath and sociopath are not formal diagnoses; both fall under antisocial personality disorder.
claims.evidence_quote: psychopath and sociopath are not formal diagnoses. Both fall under Antisocial Personality Disorder (source note 8, line 86)
claims.reasoning: Verbatim clinical caveat.

claims.claim_text: Terminology varies; empathic concern and pop-psych sympathy differ from table usage.
claims.evidence_quote: usage varies across the literature. Some authors use empathic concern roughly where this table uses compassion, and pop-psych usage treats sympathy as inherently distancing (source note 9, line 87)
claims.reasoning: Faithful compression of the terminology caveat.
